terms.meaning: The feeling of "We are One" among people of a region, with pride in it.
Early Congress leaders (1885-1905) who used prayers, appeals and protests within the law.
The extremists' mocking name for the moderates' method of begging for favours.
"Satya" (truth) + "agraha" (persuasion): standing firm on the side of truth.
Indian Muslims' support for the Turkish Caliph against Britain, led by the Ali brothers with Gandhiji.
Jinnah's claim that Hindus and Muslims were separate nations, which led to Pakistan.

items.name: Factors behind Indian nationalism
items.formula: Western education, uniform administration, economic exploitation (Naoroji's drain theory), pride in tradition, reform movements, 1857, racial discrimination (Ilbert Act, 1884).
items.example: Scholars like William Jones and Max Muller showed India's rich past.

items.name: Founding of the Indian National Congress
items.formula: 1885 in Mumbai, the idea of A. O. Hume; first President W. C. Banerjee; 72 delegates.
items.example: Aim: national unity and putting people's demands to the government.

items.name: Moderate leaders and demands
items.formula: Dadabhai Naoroji, Surendranath Banerjee, Gokhale, Ranade.
items.example: They asked for free speech, Indians in high posts, ICS exams in India, and an end to salt tax.

items.name: Extremists: Lal, Bal and Pal (1905-1919)
items.formula: Lala Lajpat Rai ("Lion of Punjab"), Tilak ("Swaraj is my birthright"), Bipin Chandra Pal.
items.example: Tilak ran Kesari and Maratha and started Ganesha and Shivaji festivals; Aurobindo pushed swadeshi.

items.name: Partition of Bengal (1905)
items.formula: Curzon split Bengal by religion; 16 October 1905 was a National Mourning Day with "Amar Sonar Bangla" and rakhis.
items.example: It was cancelled in 1911.

items.name: Muslim League and Surat split
items.formula: Muslim League founded at Dhaka in 1906 by Agha Khan and Nawab Salimullah; Congress split at Surat in 1907.
items.example: Tilak was jailed at Mandalay, where he wrote Gita Rahasya.

items.name: Rowlatt Act and Jallianwala Bagh (1919)
items.formula: The Rowlatt Act allowed arrest on suspicion alone. On 13 April 1919 General Dyer fired on a closed meeting at Amritsar.
items.example: Official count: 379 dead; the real toll was higher.

items.name: Revolutionaries
items.formula: Khudiram Bose, first martyr hanged (1908), at 19. Savarkar formed Mitramela (1899), later Abhinava Bharat.
items.example: Bhagat Singh, Rajguru and Sukhdev bombed the Central Assembly (1929); Bhagat Singh first gave "Inquilab Zindabad".

items.name: Gandhiji's early life
items.formula: Born 2 October 1869 at Porbandar; law in England; fought apartheid in South Africa.
items.example: Back in 1915, he set up Sabarmati Ashram (1916); Gokhale was his political guru.

items.name: Gandhiji's books and papers
items.formula: Influenced by the Gita, Ruskin's Unto this last and Tolstoy. He wrote My Experiments with Truth and Hind Swaraj.
items.example: His weeklies: Harijan and Young India.

items.name: Gandhiji's first struggles
items.formula: Champaran (Bihar, 1917), against forced indigo growing; Rajendra Prasad rose from it.
items.example: Kheda was another farmers' fight; the Mapillai revolt (1921) was in Malabar.

items.name: Non-Co-operation Movement (1920-22)
items.formula: Boycott of courts, schools, elections, British goods and titles; Tagore and Gandhiji returned honours.
items.example: Gandhiji called it off after Chowri-Chowra (1922), where 22 policemen were burnt.

items.name: Nehru Report and Simon Commission
items.formula: Motilal Nehru's report (1927) proposed self-rule. The all-British Simon Commission (1928) met "Go back, Simon".
items.example: Lala Lajpat Rai died after a lathi-charge at Lahore (1928).

items.name: Purna Swaraj (1929)
items.formula: The Lahore session declared complete freedom; 26 January 1930 was Purna Swarajya Day.
items.example: So the Constitution came into force on 26 January 1950, now Republic Day.

items.name: Dandi March (1930)
items.formula: Began 12 March 1930: Gandhiji and 78 followers walked 375 km from Sabarmati to Dandi to make salt.
items.example: Khan Abdul Gaffar Khan ("Frontier Gandhi") founded Khudai Khidmatgar; Ankola had a famous salt satyagraha.

items.name: Round Table Conferences (1930-32)
items.formula: Three in London; Gandhiji attended only the second.
items.example: They solved nothing; the Government of India Act followed in 1935.

items.name: Quit India Movement (1942)
items.formula: After the Cripps Mission failed, Congress met in Mumbai on 8 August 1942: "Do or Die".
items.example: Parallel governments arose in Ballia, Tamluk and Satara; Isuru (Shivamogga) declared itself independent.

items.name: Socialists and Jayaprakash Narayan
items.formula: The Congress Socialist Party (1934), with J.P. as General Secretary and Acharya Narendra Dev.
items.example: J.P. escaped from Hazaribagh jail, later led "Total Revolution" and was called "Lokanayak".

items.name: Rani Abbakkadevi of Ullala
items.formula: Of the Chowta dynasty; refused Portuguese taxes and beat them in 1555 C.E.
items.example: Betrayed by her estranged husband, she died in prison; a stamp honoured her in 2003.

items.name: Ballari Siddamma
items.formula: First woman in Mysore state to join the flag hoisting, at Shivapura (1938).
items.example: She joined the forest satyagraha and Quit India, and later became MLA of Davangere.

items.name: Kamaladevi Chattopadhyay
items.formula: With Avantibai Gokhale, the first women to break the salt law; jailed at Yerawada.
items.example: She led the Sevadal women's unit; Padma Bhushan (1955), Magsaysay Award (1966).

items.name: Yashodharamma Dasappa
items.formula: Joined the Shivapura Flag Satyagraha (1938); her house was a Quit India base.
items.example: She became an MLA, an MP and Social Welfare Minister.

items.name: Umabai Kundapur
items.formula: Wrote the Marathi play Swadeshi Vrath; led the Sevadal women's unit started by Hardekar in 1923.
items.example: She was jailed for the salt agitation and later ran the Kasturba Foundation.

items.name: Subhash Chandra Bose and the INA
items.formula: Left Congress in 1939 and founded the Forward Bloc; escaped to Germany; led the INA from Singapore (1943).
items.example: "Give me blood, I will give you freedom!"; the INA raised the tricolour on Indian soil.

items.name: Dr. B. R. Ambedkar
items.formula: Born 14 April 1891 at Mhow; led the Mahad Satyagraha; papers Mooka Nayak and Bahishkrith Bharath.
items.example: Chairman of the Drafting Committee; the Poona Pact (1932) with Gandhiji; Bharat Ratna (1990).

items.name: Jinnah and Pakistan
items.formula: Joined the Muslim League in 1913; his fourteen demands (1929); the 1940 Lahore session adopted the demand.
items.example: The name Pakistan was proposed by Chaudhary Rahamat Ali in 1933.

items.name: Independence
items.formula: On 3 June 1947 Lord Mountbatten, the last Viceroy, announced partition.
items.example: Pakistan was formed on 14 August and India became free on 15 August 1947; Nehru was the first Prime Minister.

mistakes.text: A. O. Hume founded the Congress, but its first President was W. C. Banerjee.
Two Lahore sessions: Congress's 1929 Purna Swaraj, and the Muslim League's 1940 Pakistan demand.
